response: Yes, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a place in the preoperative locoregional staging of gastric cancer. MRI can provide detailed images of the stomach and surrounding tissues, helping to assess the extent of tumor invasion, lymph node involvement, and potential spread to adjacent organs. However, its role is often complementary to other imaging modalities like computed tomography (CT) and endoscopic ultrasonography (EUS), which are more commonly used for gastric cancer staging.
